title: Create a bootable USB drive from an ISO file
summary: Use the `dd` command to write an ISO image directly to a USB drive, making it bootable. This process erases all data on the target USB drive.
prerequisites: An ISO file you want to write
A USB drive inserted into the Mac
Knowledge of the USB drive's device identifier (e.g., /dev/disk2)

steps.explain: Write the ISO file to the USB drive device. Replace <ISO_FILE> with the path to your ISO and <USB_DRIVE> with the device identifier of your USB drive (e.g., /dev/disk2). This command erases the USB drive.

placeholders.name: ISO_FILE
placeholders.description: Path to the ISO image file

placeholders.name: USB_DRIVE
placeholders.description: Device identifier of the target USB drive

steps.expect: The command will show progress as it writes data to the USB drive.

warnings: This command will completely erase all data on the target USB drive.
Double-check the device identifier (<USB_DRIVE>) to avoid overwriting your main hard drive.

rollback.explain: There is no direct rollback for `dd`. To restore the USB drive to a usable state, you must reformat it using Disk Utility.
